words.gloss: one's own heart or mind itself

literal: Do not lie about that which one's own mind knows; after lying, one's own mind itself will burn oneself.
translation: Do not tell a lie about what your own mind knows to be true; if you do lie, your own conscience will burn you.
modern: தன் மனதுக்குத் தெரிந்த உண்மையை மறைத்துப் பொய் சொல்லக் கூடாது; அப்படிப் பொய் சொன்னால், தன் மனமே தன்னை வருத்தும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of conscience in upholding truthfulness. It advises that one must never speak a lie against what their own heart or mind knows to be true. If a person goes against their inner knowledge and lies, their own conscience will continuously torment and burn them with guilt. The word 'neñcu' (heart or mind) here represents the internal witness of truth, and 'cuṭum' (will burn) vividly describes the painful heat of self-reproach.
